bank.question: If caught in a smoke-filled room, it is safer to stay low to the ground where the air is cleaner
A Fire Risk Assessment only needs to be updated if there has been a fire on the premises
bank.explanation: A Fire Risk Assessment must be reviewed regularly and immediately if there are significant changes to the building layout or occupancy
The primary piece of fire safety legislation in England and Wales is the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005
bank.question: The Health and Safety at Work Act 1974 is the only piece of legislation that covers fire safety in the UK
Proping a fire door open with a fire extinguisher or a wooden wedge is a serious breach of fire safety regulations
bank.explanation: Fire doors are designed to resist fire for a set period (usually 30 or 60 minutes) and must be kept closed to prevent the spread of smoke and flames

bank.question: A Fire Risk Assessment remains valid indefinitely as long as the building's layout does not change
bank.explanation: Under the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005, the Fire Risk Assessment must be reviewed regularly, especially if there are significant changes to the building or work activities

bank.question: A Dry Powder extinguisher with a blue label is generally considered safe for use on fires involving flammable gases (Class C)
bank.explanation: The blue label represents Dry Powder, which is often called 'multi-purpose' because it can be used on Class A, B, and C fires, as well as electrical fires
A PEEP must be specifically tailored to the individual's needs; a generic evacuation plan may not account for their specific mobility or sensory requirements
bank.question: A Personal Emergency Evacuation Plan (PEEP) should be the same for all staff members across a single company to ensure consistency
A fire blanket is the most effective piece of equipment for extinguishing a fire involving a large stack of wooden pallets
bank.explanation: Blankets are primarily used to smother small Class F (cooking oil) fires or to wrap around a person whose clothing is on fire
Smoke rises and collects at the ceiling; smoke detectors are positioned there to provide the earliest possible warning to occupants
bank.question: Smoke detectors are usually fitted to the ceiling because heat and smoke rise during a fire

bank.explanation: Class D fires involve flammable metals (e.g., magnesium or lithium) and require specialist extinguishers; liquids are Class B
bank.question: Class D fires are those involving flammable liquids such as petrol, spirits, or solvent-based paints
One of the primary duties of a Fire Warden during an evacuation is to ensure their designated area is completely clear of people
bank.explanation: Fire Wardens are responsible for checking toilets, store rooms, and other areas to ensure everyone has evacuated before reporting to the assembly point

bank.question: It is acceptable to store cardboard boxes in a fire exit corridor as long as the boxes are removed by the end of the working day
bank.explanation: By law, fire exit routes must be kept clear of all obstructions, including temporary items like deliveries or rubbish, at all times
Wet Chemical extinguishers are the only type specifically designed to safely cool and smother high-temperature cooking oil fires
bank.question: A Wet Chemical extinguisher (yellow label) is the only type of extinguisher specially designed for Class F fires

bank.explanation: The assembly point must be far enough away from the building to protect people from falling glass, smoke, and heat, and to allow space for emergency vehicles
bank.question: The designated assembly point should be located as close to the main building entrance as possible to save time during a roll call

bank.explanation: Fire safety signs in the UK must follow standardized shapes and colours: green for exits, red for equipment/prohibition, and blue for mandatory actions
bank.question: Safety signs indicating the location of fire-fighting equipment (such as extinguishers) are always red and square/rectangular in shape

bank.explanation: Carbon Dioxide (CO2) extinguishers do not have a cooling effect and are ineffective on solids; wood and paper (Class A) are best tackled with Water or Foam
bank.question: A Carbon Dioxide (CO2) fire extinguisher is the most effective choice for extinguishing a large fire involving paper and wood
The 'Fire Triangle' illustrates that removing oxygen from a fire is one of the three primary ways to extinguish it
bank.explanation: The Fire Triangle consists of Heat, Fuel, and Oxygen; removing any one of these elements will extinguish the fire

bank.question: Under the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005, a written record of a Fire Risk Assessment is only required if a business employs more than 25 people
bank.explanation: Employers with five or more employees must keep a written record of their Fire Risk Assessment
Fire doors are designed with intumescent strips and cold smoke seals to prevent the spread of lethal smoke and flames for a set period (usually 30 or 60 minutes)
bank.question: Fire doors serve a dual purpose: to provide a barrier to fire and to prevent the spread of smoke through a building

bank.explanation: The 'Stay Put' policy is common in purpose-built flats, but residents must still evacuate if their own flat is affected or if told to do so by the fire service
bank.question: In some residential blocks of flats, a 'Stay Put' policy may be in place, meaning you only evacuate if your flat is affected by fire or smoke

bank.explanation: Foam extinguishers are identified by a cream-coloured band or label; blue is used for Dry Powder
bank.question: The standard colour-coded label for a Foam fire extinguisher in the UK is blue
In a multi-storey building, the safest and fastest way to evacuate during a fire alarm is always to use the passenger lifts
bank.explanation: Lifts should never be used during a fire unless they are specifically designed 'evacuation lifts' and part of a managed PEEP
Class B fires involve flammable liquids like petrol or oil (excluding cooking oils). Foam and Dry Powder are the standard agents for these
bank.question: Class B fires involve flammable liquids and can be extinguished using a foam or dry powder extinguisher
Fire Wardens are legally required to tackle any fire they see before raising the alarm
bank.explanation: Fire wardens should only use extinguishers if they have been trained, it is safe to do so, and the alarm has already been raised

bank.question: Fire extinguishers should be clearly visible and either wall-mounted or placed on a dedicated floor stand
bank.explanation: Fire extinguishers should be mounted on the wall or kept on a stand to ensure they are visible, accessible, and not damaged
A continuous alarm usually indicates an immediate need to evacuate, whereas an intermittent tone might signal an investigation or 'standby' phase
bank.question: If a fire alarm sounds as an intermittent 'bleep', it always means the same thing as a continuous siren, and you must evacuate immediately
The 'Responsible Person' in a workplace is legally registered for ensuring the fire risk assessment is reviewed if the building layout changes
bank.explanation: The 'Responsible Person' must ensure a fire risk assessment is carried out and updated regularly, especially when significant changes occur

bank.question: Halon fire extinguishers are still commonly installed in modern UK offices as a standard fire-fighting tool
bank.explanation: Halon extinguishers were banned for general use in 2003 due to their ozone-depleting properties. Standard UK extinguishers include Water, Foam, CO2, Powder, and Wet Chemical
Water extinguishers (all-red) should never be used on electrical equipment because water conducts electricity and can lead to a fatal electric shock
bank.question: Using a standard water fire extinguisher on a fire involving live electrical equipment carries a significant risk of electric shock

bank.explanation: Door wedges should never be used to hold fire doors open, as this allows smoke and flames to spread through the building, compromising the fire compartmentation
bank.question: It is legally acceptable to use a wooden wedge to keep a fire door open during hot weather for ventilation

bank.explanation: Class C fires involve flammable gases like butane, propane, or natural gas. It is vital to isolate the gas supply before attempting to extinguish the flame
bank.question: A Class C fire specifically involves flammable gases
A PEEP (Personal Emergency Evacuation Plan) is specifically designed for individuals who may have difficulty evacuating a building unaided
bank.explanation: A Personal Emergency Evacuation Plan (PEEP) is a bespoke plan designed for an individual who may need assistance to evacuate a building safely
A fire blanket should be placed gently over the pan to smother the flames; throwing it could splash burning oil or fan the fire with a sudden gust of air
bank.question: When using a fire blanket on a chip pan fire, you should throw the blanket over the fire from a distance as quickly as possible
Fire alarm manual call points should generally be located on exit routes and at each storey exit to the street
bank.explanation: Manual Call Points (break glass units) must be located on every floor and near exits so that the alarm can be raised immediately upon discovering a fire
The Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005 applies to virtually all non-domestic premises, including the common parts of multi-occupied residential buildings
bank.question: The Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005 applies to almost all workplaces and public buildings in England and Wales
Dry Powder extinguishers are the best choice for small, unventilated hallways because the powder is harmless to breathe in
bank.explanation: Dry Powder (blue label) is versatile but creates a dense cloud that obscures vision and can cause respiratory distress, so it is often discouraged in small, confined indoor spaces

bank.question: If you discover a fire, you must attempt to extinguish it before activating the fire alarm
bank.explanation: The primary action upon discovering a fire is to raise the alarm immediately to ensure everyone can evacuate. Tackling the fire is always secondary to personal safety
The 'Responsible Person' (usually the employer or building owner) must ensure that the fire risk assessment is updated if there have been significant changes to the building or work activities
bank.question: Fire risk assessments must be reviewed if there is a reason to suspect they are no longer valid or if there has been a significant change to the premises

bank.explanation: Emergency exit signs (running man) are green and white. Red signs are used for fire-fighting equipment or 'prohibition' instructions
bank.question: Under UK safety sign regulations, an emergency exit sign should always be red to signify the urgency of the situation

bank.explanation: Class F fires (cooking oils and fats) reach extremely high temperatures; CO2 extinguishers have little cooling effect and the high-pressure discharge can splash the burning oil, spreading the fire
bank.question: A Carbon Dioxide (CO2) extinguisher is the most effective and safe choice for tackling a Class F fire involving deep-fat fryers
According to the 'Fire Triangle' principle, a fire will be extinguished if any one of its three essential elements is removed
bank.explanation: The Fire Triangle represents the three elements needed for fire: Heat, Fuel, and Oxygen. Removing even one of these elements will cause the fire to be extinguished
